title: 标普 500：AI 浪潮中的市值、基本面与估值
title_en: S&P 500: Market Value, Fundamentals and Valuation in the AI Wave
subtitle: 2023 年 5 月至 2026 年 10 月 · 研究札记
author: Taiyang Feng (Sunny)
summary: AI 相关公司的市值份额由 31.2% 升至 47.4%，公司营收份额由 14.4% 升至 20.0%。本报告对照市值、GAAP 盈利、估值、市场广度与再投资强度，保留分类、盈利质量及因果解释的边界。
summary_en: AI-related companies' share of market capitalization rose from 31.2% to 47.4%, while their share of company revenue rose from 14.4% to 20.0%. The report compares market value, GAAP earnings, valuation, breadth and reinvestment, with explicit classification, earnings-quality and causal-inference boundaries.
articleBody:
## 研究摘要：基本面增长、定价与再投资

AI 组市值增长 191.0%，公司营收增长 68.6%。营收确有领先增长，但市值扩张明显更快。动态成分与股数变化也影响总量，不能把差距全部归为估值。

GAAP 净利润增长 233.4%，PE 从 33.8 降到 29.5 倍；P/S 则从 5.0 升到 8.6 倍。利润率提升与非经营损益使两种估值信号分化。

最新 41 家 AI 公司占公司数 8.2%、市值 47.4%；前五家公司占 AI 市值 63.9%。过去一年上涨公司占比为 AI 61.0%、剩余 62.9%：总量领先不代表组内普涨。

资本开支 / 营收由 10.9% 升至 18.8%；FCF 率由 18.3% 的期内高点回落至 14.8%。这是再投资强度与现金兑现之间的张力，还不能判定投资回报好坏。

比率使用匹配样本；公司营收不等于 AI 业务收入；收益权重不同。

| 基准 → 最新 | AI 相关 | 标普整体 | 剩余公司 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 市值变化 | +191.0% | +91.4% | +46.2% |
| TTM 营收变化 | +68.6% | +21.8% | +13.9% |
| TTM GAAP 净利润变化 | +233.4% | +71.1% | +26.7% |
| 累计总收益 | +185.7% | +96.3% | +54.2% |
| 整体 PE | 33.8 → 29.5 | 23.3 → 25.9 | 20.4 → 23.3 |
| 非金融 P/S | 5.0 → 8.6 | 2.3 → 3.7 | 1.7 → 2.2 |
| 资本开支 / 营收 | 10.9% → 18.8% | 5.8% → 8.5% | 4.7% → 5.1% |
| FCF / 营收 | 12.5% → 14.8% | 8.8% → 10.2% | 8.0% → 8.7% |

## 市值与基本面：增长来自哪里

事实：AI 营收 +68.6%，剩余公司 +13.9%；AI 市值 +191.0%，GAAP 利润 +233.4%。基本面与市值都明显分化。

解释：涨幅具有已实现盈利的会计支持，但 GAAP 利润含投资重估；动态成分总量也包含组成变化，不能直接识别 AI 因果贡献。

来源：用户 CRSP / Compustat、Massive、SEC｜基准 2023-04-28 = 100；数据截至 2026-10-09，虚线为 10 月快照。

## 份额与广度：集中度不等于普涨

事实：AI 市值份额 31.2% → 47.4%，营收份额 14.4% → 20.0%，利润份额 21.5% → 41.8%。最新上涨广度 61.0%，低于剩余组 62.9%。

解释：市场价值更加集中于主题公司；AI 前五大占组内市值 63.9%。这些图尚不能分清增长由多少家公司贡献，需要后续公司层面的贡献分解。

来源：用户 CRSP / Compustat、Massive、SEC｜基准 2023-04-28 = 100；数据截至 2026-10-09，虚线为 10 月快照。

## 估值与增长：P/E 与 P/S 给出不同信号

事实：AI PE 33.8 → 29.5 倍，P/S 5.0 → 8.6 倍；最新配对营收同比 23.8%，剩余组 8.6%。

解释：市值相对营收的定价上升，相对 GAAP 利润的定价下降；不是“估值全面上升”或“现在便宜”的证据。Alphabet Q2 投资收益使净利润增加 771 亿美元。

来源：用户 CRSP / Compustat、Massive、SEC｜基准 2023-04-28 = 100；数据截至 2026-10-09，虚线为 10 月快照。

## 利润与现金：扩张需要多少再投资

事实：AI 净利率 14.8% → 29.3%，资本开支率 10.9% → 18.8%；FCF 率从 2024-06 的 18.3% 回落至 14.8%，仍高于初始 12.5%。

解释：会计盈利与现金生成可能分化；再投资强度上升与 FCF 率回落同时出现，但固定样本和公司层面检验前，不能把全部回落归因于 AI 资本开支。

## 结论：

这份研究的核心发现是自2023 年 4 月以来，标普 500 中 41 家 AI 相关公司的市值上涨 191%，同期营收增长 68.6%、GAAP 净利润增长 233.4%，其市值占比从 31.2% 升至 47.4%，利润占比从 21.5% 升至 41.8%。对数分解显示，累计收益中约 120 个百分点来自利润增长，估值贡献为负（约 -13 个百分点），说明这一轮上涨主要由盈利兑现驱动，而非单纯的倍数扩张。整体 PE 则由 33.8 倍降至 29.5 倍，与"泡沫"叙事并不吻合。不过需要注意，利润增长中近一半来自净利率翻倍（14.8% 升至 29.3%），而非营收扩张本身，这使得估值合理性高度依赖净利率的可持续性。

但盈利质量与集中度是两处需要折价看待的地方。其一，GAAP 利润含大量非经营性投资收益，仅 Alphabet 单季 771 亿美元的股权投资收益，就使 AI 组 PE 从 29.5 倍上调至 31.7 倍；与此同时，P/S 从 5.0 升至 8.6 倍，说明市场对营收的定价显著抬高，PE 下降并不等于"变便宜"。其二，净利率翻倍而 FCF 率仅从 12.5% 升至 14.8%（且自 2024 年中的 18.3% 高点回落），叠加资本开支占营收比由 10.9% 升至 18.8%，账面利润向现金的转化率明显下降，这是典型的"重投入期"特征。再加上前五大公司占组内市值 63.9%、组内上涨家数占比（61.0%）反而低于其余公司（62.9%），"AI 组"的表现很可能主要是少数巨头的表现。综合来看，我们认为 AI 主题的基本面支撑是实的，但市场已经为高利润率的持续和资本开支的最终回报定下了较高预期；在去头部检验、经营性利润调整和现金回报分析完成之前，更稳妥的立场是：不否定主题，但对"估值合理"的结论保持克制。

来源：用户 CRSP / Compustat、Massive、SEC｜基准 2023-04-28 = 100；数据截至 2026-10-09，虚线为 10 月快照。

## 方法、分类对照与必要边界

广义 AI + 历史退出公司：41 家，市值份额 47.4%，营收份额 20.0%，累计研究组合收益 185.7%。

固定 41 家广义 AI：41 家，市值份额 47.4%，营收份额 20.0%，累计研究组合收益 186.8%。

固定 29 家直接 AI：29 家，市值份额 46.0%，营收份额 18.5%，累计研究组合收益 190.8%。

研究期为 2023 年 5 月至 2026-10-09，基准 2023-04-28，完整月末至 2026-09。历史成分随生效事件变化；股份类别归并到公司。股数与成分变化会影响市值及基本面总量。

主分类为 41 家广义参考，加 ANSS、JNPR、EPAM、TTD、DXC、DAY/CDAY、PAYC 七家历史退出补充；补充标签从商业化业务证据生效后、且公司实际在指数内时使用。参考名单为回顾性标签，剩余公司不等于没有 AI 敞口。

市值为上市普通股总额，非官方自由流通市值。PE 包含亏损及 GAAP 非经营损益；P/S、净利率、资本开支率、FCF 率为非金融匹配样本。图 16 在紧凑版展示最新累计对数分解；独立图保留完整月度四面板曲线。

最新 AI 营收 / 净利润市值覆盖 100% / 100%；整体约 99.4% / 99.4%。AI 资本开支率 / FCF 率约 98.2% / 98.2%，整体 92.8% / 92.7%。各图附最低 / 最新覆盖率。分类、退出、缺口与两源差异明细在随附工作簿 / 审计文件，原第 25 页和第 26 页不再单列。

AI / 剩余为上市普通股市值加权月度再平衡组合，整体为官方标普总收益指数；权重不同、未计交易成本。固定公司同比使用当期成员的前后 TTM 配对。历史盈利预期按要求排除。

## 盈利质量、来源与后续验证

Alphabet 2026 Q2 原始公告披露，股权证券净收益使净利润增加 771 亿美元。仅机械剔除这一项，AI 组最新 PE 约由 29.5 升至 31.7 倍；这只是一项敏感性示意，不是完整经营性利润调整。不能把 GAAP 净利润曲线直接当作 AI 核心经营盈利曲线。

现有图表支持“主题公司的营收、利润和市场价值同时增长，并伴随更高再投资强度”。它们尚不能回答：增长有多少来自 AI 业务；去除头部公司后是否仍成立；投入的最终现金回报是否达到市场要求。

优先扩展三项验证：按公司分解营收、利润及收益贡献，检验头部集中；补充经营利润与非经营损益调整；将直接 AI、电力、设备分层，配对资本开支、经营现金流和回报。以上是后续研究方向，不代表本版已完成。

## 参考来源

- [历史成分种子与官方复核](https://github.com/fja05680/sp500)

- [SEC Company Facts](https://www.sec.gov/search-filings/edgar-application-programming-interfaces)

articleBody_en:
## Research Summary: Fundamentals, Pricing and Reinvestment

The AI group's market capitalization rose 191.0%, versus 68.6% growth in company revenue. Revenue growth clearly outpaced the rest of the index, but market value expanded considerably faster. Changes in constituents and share counts also affect aggregates; the entire gap cannot be attributed to valuation.

GAAP net income rose 233.4%, and aggregate P/E fell from 33.8 to 29.5 times, while P/S rose from 5.0 to 8.6 times. Higher profit margins and non-operating gains create divergent valuation signals.

The latest 41 AI companies represent 8.2% of companies and 47.4% of market capitalization. The five largest account for 63.9% of AI market value. Over the past year, 61.0% of AI companies rose, versus 62.9% of the remaining companies. Aggregate outperformance does not imply broad gains within the group.

Capital expenditure / revenue rose from 10.9% to 18.8%, while the free cash flow margin fell from its within-period peak of 18.3% to 14.8%. This reveals tension between reinvestment intensity and cash realization; it does not yet establish whether investment returns are good or poor.

Ratios use matched samples. Company revenue is not AI business revenue. Return weighting differs between the groups and the index.

| Base to latest | AI-related | S&P 500 | Remaining companies |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Market value change | +191.0% | +91.4% | +46.2% |
| TTM revenue change | +68.6% | +21.8% | +13.9% |
| TTM GAAP net income change | +233.4% | +71.1% | +26.7% |
| Cumulative total return | +185.7% | +96.3% | +54.2% |
| Aggregate P/E | 33.8 → 29.5 | 23.3 → 25.9 | 20.4 → 23.3 |
| Non-financial P/S | 5.0 → 8.6 | 2.3 → 3.7 | 1.7 → 2.2 |
| Capex / revenue | 10.9% → 18.8% | 5.8% → 8.5% | 4.7% → 5.1% |
| FCF / revenue | 12.5% → 14.8% | 8.8% → 10.2% | 8.0% → 8.7% |

## Market Value and Fundamentals: Sources of Growth

Facts: AI revenue rose 68.6%, versus 13.9% for the remaining companies. AI market value rose 191.0% and GAAP earnings 233.4%. Both fundamentals and market value diverged substantially.

Interpretation: Reported earnings provide accounting support for the gains, but GAAP earnings include investment revaluations. Aggregates for changing constituents also reflect composition effects and cannot directly identify AI's causal contribution.

Sources: User-provided CRSP / Compustat, Massive and SEC. Base: 2023-04-28 = 100. Data through 2026-10-09; dashed segments denote the October snapshot.

## Shares and Breadth: Concentration Is Not Broad Participation

Facts: AI market value share rose from 31.2% to 47.4%, revenue share from 14.4% to 20.0%, and earnings share from 21.5% to 41.8%. Latest advancing breadth is 61.0%, below the remaining group's 62.9%.

Interpretation: Market value is increasingly concentrated in thematic companies. The five largest account for 63.9% of AI market capitalization. These charts cannot yet determine how many companies drive the growth; company-level contribution analysis is needed.

Sources: User-provided CRSP / Compustat, Massive and SEC. Base: 2023-04-28 = 100. Data through 2026-10-09; dashed segments denote the October snapshot.

## Valuation and Growth: P/E and P/S Send Different Signals

Facts: AI P/E fell from 33.8 to 29.5 times, while P/S rose from 5.0 to 8.6 times. Latest matched-company revenue growth is 23.8% year on year, versus 8.6% for the remaining group.

Interpretation: Pricing relative to revenue increased, while pricing relative to GAAP earnings fell. This is not evidence that valuations rose across the board or that the group is now cheap. Alphabet's Q2 investment gains increased net income by $77.1 billion.

Sources: User-provided CRSP / Compustat, Massive and SEC. Base: 2023-04-28 = 100. Data through 2026-10-09; dashed segments denote the October snapshot.

## Earnings and Cash: The Reinvestment Behind Expansion

Facts: AI net margin rose from 14.8% to 29.3%, and capital expenditure / revenue from 10.9% to 18.8%. The FCF margin fell from 18.3% in June 2024 to 14.8%, still above its initial 12.5%.

Interpretation: Accounting earnings and cash generation can diverge. Higher reinvestment intensity coincides with a lower FCF margin, but the entire decline cannot be attributed to AI capital expenditure before fixed-sample and company-level tests are completed.

## Conclusion

The central finding is that, since April 2023, the market capitalization of 41 AI-related S&P 500 companies rose 191%, alongside 68.6% revenue growth and 233.4% GAAP net income growth. Their market value share increased from 31.2% to 47.4%, and their earnings share from 21.5% to 41.8%. The logarithmic decomposition attributes about 120 percentage points of cumulative return to earnings growth, with a negative valuation contribution of roughly 13 percentage points. This suggests that realized earnings, rather than multiple expansion alone, were the main accounting driver of the rise. Aggregate P/E fell from 33.8 to 29.5 times, which does not align neatly with a bubble narrative. However, almost half of the earnings expansion came from a doubling of net margin, from 14.8% to 29.3%, rather than revenue growth itself. The case for reasonable valuation therefore depends heavily on the sustainability of those margins.

Earnings quality and concentration are two reasons to apply a discount to that interpretation. First, GAAP earnings contain substantial non-operating investment gains. Mechanically excluding Alphabet's $77.1 billion equity investment gain in a single quarter raises the AI group's P/E from 29.5 to 31.7 times. Meanwhile, P/S rose from 5.0 to 8.6 times, indicating materially higher pricing of revenue; a lower P/E does not necessarily mean the group became cheaper. Second, while net margin doubled, the FCF margin rose only from 12.5% to 14.8% and fell from its mid-2024 peak of 18.3%. Together with the rise in capital expenditure / revenue from 10.9% to 18.8%, this indicates a marked decline in the conversion of accounting profits into cash, characteristic of a heavy investment phase. The five largest companies account for 63.9% of group market value, and advancing breadth of 61.0% is below the remaining companies' 62.9%. The AI group's performance may therefore be driven mainly by a few giants. Taken together, we see real fundamental support for the AI theme, but market prices already embed high expectations for sustained margins and the eventual returns on capital expenditure. Until tests excluding the largest companies, operating-earnings adjustments and cash-return analysis are completed, the more measured stance is to recognize the theme while remaining cautious about claims that valuation is reasonable.

Sources: User-provided CRSP / Compustat, Massive and SEC. Base: 2023-04-28 = 100. Data through 2026-10-09; dashed segments denote the October snapshot.

## Methodology, Classification Comparisons and Boundaries

Broad AI plus historical exits: 41 companies; market capitalization share 47.4%; revenue share 20.0%; cumulative research portfolio return 185.7%.

Fixed set of 41 broad AI companies: 41 companies; market capitalization share 47.4%; revenue share 20.0%; cumulative research portfolio return 186.8%.

Fixed set of 29 direct AI companies: 29 companies; market capitalization share 46.0%; revenue share 18.5%; cumulative research portfolio return 190.8%.

The study runs from May 2023 through October 9, 2026, with April 28, 2023 as the base date and complete month-ends through September 2026. Historical membership changes with effective index events, and share classes are consolidated at company level. Changes in share counts and constituents affect market value and fundamental aggregates.

The main classification consists of 41 broad reference companies, supplemented by seven historical exits: ANSS, JNPR, EPAM, TTD, DXC, DAY/CDAY and PAYC. Supplementary labels apply only after evidence of commercial activity becomes effective and while the company is actually in the index. The reference list is a retrospective label; the remaining companies are not necessarily without AI exposure.

Market capitalization covers listed common equity, rather than official free-float value. P/E includes losses and GAAP non-operating gains or losses. P/S, net margin, capital expenditure / revenue and FCF margin use matched non-financial samples. Figure 16 presents the latest cumulative logarithmic decomposition in this compact edition; the standalone figure retains the full monthly four-panel series.

Latest market-cap-weighted coverage for AI revenue / net income is 100% / 100%, versus approximately 99.4% / 99.4% for the full index. AI capital expenditure / revenue and FCF margin coverage is approximately 98.2% / 98.2%, versus 92.8% / 92.7% overall. Each chart states minimum / latest coverage. Classification, exits, missing fields and differences between sources are detailed in the accompanying workbook / audit files; the original pages 25 and 26 are no longer shown separately.

AI and remaining-company portfolios use listed-common-equity market-cap weights with monthly rebalancing; the full-index benchmark is the official S&P total return index. Weights differ and transaction costs are excluded. Matched-company year-on-year growth pairs current members' earlier and later TTM values. Historical earnings expectations are excluded as requested.

## Earnings Quality, Sources and Further Validation

Alphabet's original Q2 2026 release reports that net gains on equity securities increased net income by $77.1 billion. Mechanically excluding only this item raises the AI group's latest P/E from about 29.5 to 31.7 times. This is a single-item sensitivity illustration, not a complete adjustment to operating earnings. The GAAP net income series cannot be treated directly as a series of core AI operating earnings.

The existing charts support simultaneous growth in thematic companies' revenue, earnings and market value, alongside higher reinvestment intensity. They do not yet establish how much growth came from AI business, whether the findings survive excluding the largest companies, or whether eventual cash returns on investment will meet market expectations.

Three tests take priority: decompose company-level contributions to revenue, earnings and returns to assess concentration; add operating-earnings and non-operating-item adjustments; and separate direct AI, power and equipment, matching capital expenditure, operating cash flow and returns. These are directions for further research, not analyses completed in this edition.
